global_issues.title: Brent crude tops $101 on Iran conflict escalation
global_issues.note: Confirmed by CNBC, Al Jazeera, TheStreet, OilPrice.com — Brent broke $100 on Sept 9 2026 amid US-Iran strikes on tankers/shipping, reaching intraday levels near/above $101. However, the briefing's 'highest since May' detail is wrong: multiple sources (OilPrice, TradingEconomics, CNBC) say this is the highest level since July 24, 2026, not May. Conflict has since escalated further; Goldman Sachs warns of $120/bbl risk.

global_issues.title: Treasury $6B buyback sparks yield spike, disappoints market
global_issues.note: Confirmed by CNBC, Reuters, Yahoo Finance, Treasury.gov press release: $6B buyback of 10-20yr debt announced Sept 9 for the Sept 10 operation, triple the normal size. 10-year yield hit 4.85% (highest since Nov 2023), 20-year 5.31%, 30-year 5.31%. Yields rose despite/because of the buyback, matching the briefing's framing.

missing_major_news.title: Meta (META) rallied ~6.5% on Sept 9 while broader market fell, described by outlets as 'decoupling' from macro headwinds with institutional buying
missing_major_news.impact: META — briefing's watchlist entry captures the price move (+6.55%) and 'optimistic' mood, but the sector/mood summary lists META only as a DISTRIBUTION laggard pressured by yields, without noting it was the standout gainer of the day, which is a notable narrative gap.

stock_errors.error: Labeled DISTRIBUTION and grouped with other 'long-duration growth names' under yield pressure in the market mood summary, but real reporting shows META was the outlier gainer (+6.55%, consistent with the briefing's own watchlist price) on institutional buying, decoupled from the macro pressure — the mood narrative doesn't reconcile the contradiction between trend label and price action.

grok_report.summary: The two global issues are directionally accurate and well-sourced (Brent >$100 on Iran escalation, $6B Treasury buyback triggering a yield spike to multi-year highs), but the briefing's claim that oil is at its 'highest since May' is factually wrong — real sources put it at highest since July 24. Market mood and sector rotation calls align well with actual Sept 9 index/sector performance. The main soft spot is an internal inconsistency around META (DISTRIBUTION label vs. its actual outlier rally), and a few minor upcoming catalysts (NVDA at Goldman conference, Apple event) aren't flagged.
